title: People's Republic of Kampuchea

endonym.native: សាធារណរដ្ឋប្រជាមានិតកម្ពុជា

capsule: The People's Republic of Kampuchea was a Vietnamese-backed state established on 7 January 1979, the day Vietnamese forces and Cambodian defectors captured Phnom Penh and expelled the Khmer Rouge regime of Democratic Kampuchea. Led by Heng Samrin as head of state and guided closely by Vietnamese advisers, the PRK rebuilt state institutions and implemented a controlled collectivisation, though famine conditions persisted into 1979–1980. Despite Soviet recognition, the United States, China, and ASEAN nations blocked its UN membership, allowing the Khmer Rouge to retain Cambodia's UN seat throughout the 1980s. In 1989 the regime renamed itself the State of Cambodia, abandoned Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy, and Vietnamese troops withdrew; a UN transitional administration (UNTAC) oversaw elections in 1993.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The PRK's territory corresponded to most of present-day Cambodia and is well documented; areas near the Thai border were contested by Khmer Rouge remnants throughout the 1980s.
